comparison.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop, then verifies retained motion; PR-2241 levels a sand bed by pulling a screed board along rails.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench seating, countertorque, and preserving a screw setting while tightening a jam nut. PR-2241 requires bimanual board transport, rail contact, synchronized pulling, and controlled material redistribution.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate grades locked 90° opening accuracy, low drift across three cycles, hardware retention, and released clearance. PR-2241 grades a bridged pull, sand-depth flatness, lack of post-pass disturbance, board stowage, and release. Both include hands-off checks, but their functional outcomes differ.
comparison.reason: The tested abilities are meaningfully different: coupled screw-and-locknut adjustment with retained articulated calibration versus guided screeding of bulk material. Both available spec versions were read and provide complete numeric rubrics; no material rubric detail is missing.
